info.title: Tidepool API (1Click-compatible, testnet)
info.description: Community-built testnet sandbox for NEAR Intents. Unaffiliated with NEAR or 1Click. Request and response shapes for every /v0 endpoint follow the public 1Click Swap API OpenAPI v0.1.10 (https://1click.chaindefuser.com/docs/v0/openapi.yaml) so that switching the base URL is enough. Testnet tokens only; they have no value.

post.description:
Verifies wallet signature and issues session tokens

Tidepool: free JWTs (HS256, access 1 h, refresh 30 d), valid on Tidepool only. Supported standards: nep413, raw_ed25519, erc191. The key must belong to the signer (NEAR implicit account, a NEAR access key, or a key registered on the verifier).

Exchange refresh token for a new access token

Tidepool: exchanges a refresh token for a new access token.

get.description:
Returns token balances for the authenticated user from private balance sources

Tidepool: needs a Tidepool JWT (401 without). Balances come from the testnet verifier; source is `private`.

parameters.name: tokenIds
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of token IDs to query. If empty, returns all non-zero balances.

get.description:
Returns paginated public and confidential transaction history. History is invite-only for now. For the initial request, omit both nextCursor and prevCursor to retrieve the latest history. For subsequent requests, pass either nextCursor or prevCursor from the previous response.

Tidepool: needs a Tidepool JWT. Swaps where you are the refund address or recipient, newest first, with cursor paging.

get.description:
Retrieves a list of tokens currently supported by the 1Click API for asset swaps.

Each token entry includes its blockchain, contract address (if available), price in USD, and other metadata such as symbol and decimals.

Native ETH is listed for eth, base and arb (assetIds nep141:eth.tp-omft.testnet, nep141:base.tp-omft.testnet, nep141:arb.tp-omft.testnet; 18 decimals, no contractAddress) and is capped at 0.01 ETH per swap.

parameters.name: ondoTokens
parameters.description: Show Ondo tokens if the query is set

post.description:
Generates a swap quote based on input parameters such as the assets, amount, slippage tolerance, and recipient/refund information.

Returns pricing details, estimated time, and a unique **deposit address** to which tokens must be transferred to initiate the swap.

You can set the `dry` parameter to `true` to simulate the quote request **without generating a deposit address** or initiating the swap process. This is useful for previewing swap parameters or validating input data without committing to an actual swap.

This endpoint is the first required step in the swap process. Tidepool supports EXACT_INPUT, EXACT_OUTPUT, FLEX_INPUT and ANY_INPUT; appFees; depositMode SIMPLE and MEMO (MEMO for NEAR-native ORIGIN_CHAIN only); ORIGIN_CHAIN and INTENTS deposit/refund types; DESTINATION_CHAIN and INTENTS recipient types. CONFIDENTIAL_INTENTS / confidentiality is accepted but ignored. Tidepool-only: the optional `simulate` field (`STUCK` or `FAILED`) simulates a stuck or failed swap on testnet; see the Testing failure cases guide. Native ETH on Ethereum, Base and Arbitrum Sepolia (nep141:eth.tp-omft.testnet, nep141:base.tp-omft.testnet, nep141:arb.tp-omft.testnet, like 1Click's nep141:eth.omft.near, base.omft.near, arb.omft.near) is delivery only and capped at 0.01 ETH (10000000000000000 wei) per swap, payout or refund: a larger ETH leg answers 400 at quote time, and payouts answer 503 while the treasury is low. Native ETH cannot be an ORIGIN_CHAIN deposit and ANY_INPUT payouts are rejected.

Retrieves the current status of a swap using the unique deposit address from the quote, if quote response included deposit memo, it is required as well.

The response includes the state of the swap (e.g., pending, processing, success, refunded) and any associated swap and transaction details.

Optionally notifies the 1Click service that a deposit has been sent to the specified address, using the blockchain transaction hash.

This step can speed up swap processing by allowing the system to preemptively verify the deposit.

post.description:
Generates an unsigned intent payload that needs to be signed by the user.

  This endpoint takes a quote or limit-order deposit address, validates the target state and caller ownership when required, and returns an intent payload formatted according to the specified signing standard (e.g., NEP413, ERC191).

  The generated intent must be signed by the user's wallet and then submitted via the `/submit-intent` endpoint to complete the action (e.g. swap).

  **Request Type Variants:**
  - `swap_transfer`: Generate an intent for a swap operation (requires depositAddress, signerId, standard)

Tidepool: only quotes with depositType INTENTS can be funded this way. Supports nep413, raw_ed25519, erc191, tip191 and sep53. webauthn and ton_connect are accepted by submit-intent but cannot be generated.

post.description:
Submits a signed intent to execute.

  After generating an intent for a quote or limit order via `/generate-intent` and having the user sign it with their wallet, submit the signed intent through this endpoint.

  The system validates the signature, processes the intent, and returns the intent hash upon successful submission.

  **Request Type Variants:**
  - `swap_transfer`: Submit a signed swap intent (requires signedData object)

Tidepool: relays the signed intent to the testnet verifier with execute_intents. The response adds `tidepool.txHash` and `tidepool.explorerUrl`.

post.description:
Creates a confidential order.

**Errors.** Branch on `code`, never on `title` or `detail`. New codes arrive without a major
version, so treat an unrecognized code as the HTTP status alone.

| Status | Codes |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | `malformed-request`, `validation-failed`, `request-rejected`, `order-rejected` |
| 401 | `authentication-required` |
| 403 | `client-generated-id` |
| 409 | `resource-type-mismatch` |
| 429 | `rate-limit-exceeded` |
| 500 | `internal-error` |
| 503 | `service-unavailable` |

Tidepool: needs a Tidepool JWT or any X-API-Key. The Tidepool maker fills the whole order once (no partial fills). SELL fills at the limit price. `confidentiality` is ignored. The deadline defaults to 7 days, max 30.

id.description: Opaque resource identifier. Clients should treat IDs as opaque and not rely on the prefix or length.

post.summary: Get testnet tokens (Tidepool extension, not part of 1Click)
post.description: Drips Tidepool test tokens; the same faucet backs the dropdown on /docs/guides/faucet. NEAR (no chain): pass accountId; mode=wallet mints the six NEP-141 test tokens to the account; mode=intents credits them inside the Tidepool verifier. With mode=intents, assets also accepts chain aliases (sol, stellar, sui, base, arb, eth, bridged) that credit that chain's bridged test tokens to the intents balance: USDC and USDT 100 each, plus verifier-only test SOL (0.05) for sol and test XLM (5) for stellar and test SUI (0.5) for sui; bridged drips have their own hourly limit. Other chains: pass chain (eth, base, arb, sol, stellar or sui) and the address on that chain to send 100 test USDC and 100 test USDT there (ERC-20, SPL with token accounts created for you, Stellar classic assets, or Sui Move coins (no setup, any address); Stellar needs an existing account with trustlines to issuer GDXABUSRHP4YA5CELHLNJQ4M3TX2BSJ6PEMDFCG2RA4PQLAQLRMFFQAN). Native gas (ETH, SOL, XLM, SUI) is never dripped: use each chain's own faucet. Native BTC (testnet4) and native XRP are never dripped either: chain btc and chain xrp answer 400 and name the external faucet (CypherFaucet / testnet4.info for BTC, the official XRPL testnet faucet faucet.altnet.rippletest.net for XRP). One drip per account (or address) and mode/chain per hour; 6 per IP per hour.

accountId.description: NEAR testnet account. Required unless chain/address are set.

assets.description: Optional subset: asset ids, NEAR symbols, or (mode=intents) chain aliases sol, stellar, sui, base, arb, eth, bridged (btc and xrp are accepted but give nothing: native BTC and XRP are never dripped). Default: the six NEAR tokens.

chain.description: Chain to drip USDC and USDT on (Base Sepolia, Arbitrum Sepolia, Ethereum Sepolia, Solana devnet, Stellar testnet, Sui testnet). Omit for NEAR. btc and xrp are not drip chains: they answer 400 with the external faucet to use (native BTC and XRP are never dripped).

address.description: Address on that chain: 0x… (eth, base, arb), base58 (sol), G… (stellar) or 0x + 64 hex (sui). Required with chain.

post.summary: Run the full demo flow in one call (Tidepool extension)
post.description: Runs the whole 1Click flow on NEAR testnet in one call, with no key and no clone. The server uses an already-funded demo account whose key stays server-side and is never returned. `flow: swap` does tokens, dry quote, live quote, generate-intent, signed submit-intent, deposit/submit, status polling until final, authenticate, balances and history (1 USDC to USDT, INTENTS deposit). `flow: order` creates a LIMIT order (SELL 1 USDC at 1.5), funds it, reads it as it goes OPEN, cancels it and shows the refund. `all` (default) does both. The response is a JSON step log: every step has the exact public request (method, url, headers, body with signatures and tokens redacted), the real response and timing, plus explorer links to the real transactions. Amounts are fixed. Limits: 3 runs per hour per IP, 20 per hour in total, one run at a time, 150 s timeout. Runs take roughly 30 to 90 s, so set your client timeout to at least 180 s. Tidepool extension, not part of 1Click.

recipient.description: Confidential Intents account identifier that receives this rebate share. Rebate delivery uses signed transfer intent on Confidential Intents; direct token transfers are not supported.

recipient.description: Account ID within Intents to which this fee will be transferred

fee.description: Fee for this recipient as part of amountIn in basis points (1/100th of a percent), e.g. 100 for 1% fee

dry.description:
Flag indicating whether this is a dry run request.
If `true`, the response will **NOT** contain the following fields:
- `depositAddress`
- `timeWhenInactive`
- `deadline`

depositMode.description:
What deposit address mode you will get in the response, most chain supports only `SIMPLE` and some(for example `stellar`) only `MEMO`:
- `SIMPLE` - usual deposit with only deposit address.
- `MEMO` - some chains will **REQUIRE** the `memo` together with `depositAddress` for swap to work.

`depositMode` applies only to deposit transaction metadata.

swapType.description:
How to interpret `amount` (and refunds) when performing the swap:

- `EXACT_INPUT` — requests the output amount for an exact input.
  - If deposit is less than `amountIn`, the deposit is refunded by deadline.
  - If deposit is above than `amountIn`, the swap is processed and the excess is refunded to `refundTo` address after swap is complete.

- `EXACT_OUTPUT` — requests the input amount for an exact output.
  - The output amount (`amountOut`) is fixed; slippage is applied to the **input** side.
  - The quote response includes `amountIn` (the proposed input with slippage tolerance baked in) and `minAmountIn` (the minimum input required).
  - **Important**: `amountIn` will appear higher than `minAmountIn` by approximately your `slippageTolerance`. This is **not** price degradation—it is a buffer to ensure successful execution. Any input amount above what is actually needed for the swap is **refunded** to your `refundTo` address after the swap completes.
  - If the deposit is above `amountIn`, the swap is processed and the excess is refunded to `refundTo` address after swap is complete.
  - If the deposit is less than `minAmountIn`, the deposit is refunded by deadline.

- `FLEX_INPUT` — a flexible input amount that allows for partial deposits and variable amounts.
  - `slippage` applies both to `amountOut` and `amountIn` and defines an acceptable range (`minAmountIn` and `minAmountOut`).
  - Any amount higher than `minAmountIn` is accepted and converted to the output asset as long as `minAmountOut` is met.
  - The deposit must be at least `minAmountIn`, after applying the slippage constraint to the quoted amount. Deposits below `minAmountIn` are refunded if the total received by the deadline is below this amount.
  - If deposits exceed the upper bound, the swap is still processed

- `ANY_INPUT` — collects deposits and converts them to a destination asset. Used for fee aggregation and similar use cases. Only available for authorized partners.

slippageTolerance.description: Slippage tolerance for the swap. This value is in basis points (1/100th of a percent), e.g. 100 for 1% slippage.

depositType.description:
Type of deposit address:
- `ORIGIN_CHAIN` - deposit address on the origin chain.
- `INTENTS` - the account ID within NEAR Intents to which you should transfer assets.
- `CONFIDENTIAL_INTENTS` - the account ID within Confidential Intents to which assets are to be transferred. Fund the swap from a Confidential Intents account by submitting a signed transfer intent to the quote `depositAddress`. Direct token transfers are not supported.

amount.description: Amount to swap as the base amount. It is interpreted as the input or output amount based on the `swapType` flag and is specified in the smallest unit of the currency (e.g., wei for ETH). Must be an integer string; decimal values like "0.01" are invalid—use base units (e.g. "10000000000000000" for 0.01 with 18 decimals).

refundType.description:
Type of refund address:
- `ORIGIN_CHAIN` - assets are refunded to the `refundTo` address on the origin chain.
- `INTENTS` - assets are refunded to the `refundTo` Intents account.
- `CONFIDENTIAL_INTENTS` - assets are refunded to the `refundTo` Confidential Intents account. On Confidential Intents, 1Click settles refunds via signed transfer intent rather than direct token transfer.

recipient.description: Recipient address. The format must match `recipientType`. Destination routing metadata, when required, must be encoded according to the destination chain address format.

virtualChainRecipient.description: EVM address of a transfer recipient in a virtual chain

virtualChainRefundRecipient.description: EVM address of a refund recipient in a virtual chain

customRecipientMsg.description:
**HIGHLY EXPERIMENTAL** Message to pass to `ft_transfer_call` when withdrawing assets to NEAR.

Otherwise, `ft_transfer` will be used.

**WARNING**: Funds will be lost if used with non NEP-141 tokens, in case of insufficient `storage_deposit` or if the recipient does not implement `ft_on_transfer` method.

recipientType.description:
Type of recipient address:
- `DESTINATION_CHAIN` - assets are transferred to the chain of `destinationAsset`.
- `INTENTS` - assets are transferred to an account inside Intents.
- `CONFIDENTIAL_INTENTS` - assets are transferred to the `recipient` account inside Confidential Intents. On Confidential Intents, 1Click settles swap output via signed transfer intent rather than direct token transfer.

deadline.description: Timestamp in ISO format that identifies when the user refund begins if the swap isn't completed by then. It must exceed the time required for the deposit transaction to be mined. For example, Bitcoin may require around one hour depending on the fees paid.

confidentiality.description: Confidentiality mode for this quote. PUBLIC is the default; BASIC or ADVANCED request Confidential Intents handling.

simulate.description: **Tidepool-only, testnet-only, optional.** Real 1Click has no such field; omit it and Tidepool behaves like 1Click. Simulates a swap outage after the deposit is detected. `STUCK`: the swap goes to `PROCESSING` and stays there until `deadline`, then the origin token is refunded to `refundTo` (`REFUNDED`, `refundReason: DEADLINE_PASSED`). `FAILED`: the swap goes to `PROCESSING`, then `FAILED`, and the deposit is refunded (`refundReason: SWAP_FAILED`, `refundedAmount` set). Other values return HTTP 400. Not supported with `ANY_INPUT`. The flag is stored with the quote and reported as `tidepool.simulate` in `/v0/status`. It reproduces what a client sees when 1Click is slow or down, not the cause. Remove it when you move to mainnet 1Click.

referral.description: Distribution channel / venue identifier (for example: ledger, trustwallet). Keep lowercase for consistency.

rebates.description: Rebate distribution for this quote. Provide up to 3 confidential Intents recipients (for example, `rebate-recipient.near` on confidential Intents); each item defines a recipient and its percent share, and all shares must add up to 100.

quoteWaitingTimeMs.description:
Time in milliseconds the user is willing to wait for a quote from the relay.
**Defaults to 0ms delay if not specified, if you want to receive the fastest quote.

appFees.description: List of recipients and their fees

insured.description: Opt into an insured swap. When `true`, an additional 0.02% (2 basis points) insurance fee is charged on top of any other fees.

blockchain.description: Blockchain on which this deposit address accepts funds for the quote.

address.description: Deposit address on `blockchain`. Funds sent here are credited to the same Intents account.

memo.description: Memo required together with `address` on chains that need it (e.g. Stellar, XRP, TON).

depositAddress.description:
The deposit address on the chain of `originAsset` when `depositType` is `ORIGIN_CHAIN`.

The deposit address inside NEAR Intents (the verifier smart contract) when `depositType` is `INTENTS`.

The account ID within Confidential Intents to which assets are to be transferred when `depositType` is `CONFIDENTIAL_INTENTS`. Fund the swap by submitting a signed transfer intent to this value. Direct token transfers are not supported.

depositMemo.description: Some deposit addresses **REQUIRE** a `memo` together with `depositAddress` for the deposit to be processed. This field is deposit-side metadata.

chainDepositAddresses.description: Deposit addresses across all bridge-supported blockchains for funding the same Intents account. Present only for public `ANY_INPUT` quotes (`depositType` `INTENTS`); the confidential rail does not support multi-chain funding addresses yet. Each entry forwards to the Intents account in `depositAddress`, so the user may deposit from any listed chain.

side.description: Order side. SELL spends the base asset; BUY spends the quote asset.

depositType.description: ORIGIN_CHAIN returns a chain address; INTENTS and CONFIDENTIAL_INTENTS use the generate-intent and submit-intent flow.

recipient.description: Address or Intents account that receives successfully filled output.

deadline.description: Timestamp in ISO format that identifies when the order can expire.

timeInForce.description: Time in force for the order.

appFees.description: Application fees included in the submitted limit price and deducted from input.

withdrawal.description: Latest successful withdrawal, or current withdrawal when none succeeded.

allWithdrawals.description: All successful withdrawals, ordered from oldest to newest.

refund.description: Main refund, or null when no refund exists.

id.description: Public identifier for this fill attempt.

amountIn.description: Gross input allocated to the fill, in input-asset smallest units.

amountOut.description: Net output received for the fill, in output-asset smallest units.

depositAddress.description: Deposit address for funding the order.

depositMemo.description: Memo to include with the deposit, when required.

fillStatus.description: Current fill status. This does not show whether payout funds arrived.

payoutStatus.description: Aggregated progress of the main withdrawal and refund.

isPayoutStatusFinal.description: Whether payoutStatus is COMPLETED or FAILED. This field is derived and has no additional meaning.

depositedAmount.description: Cumulative deposited input amount in the smallest unit of the base asset for SELL or the quote asset for BUY.

depositedAmountFormatted.description: Cumulative deposited input amount formatted using the input asset decimals.

baseAsset.description: ID of the base asset in the trading pair.

quoteAsset.description: ID of the quote asset used to price the base asset.

quantity.description: Base-asset order quantity in the asset smallest unit. A BUY targets this output; a SELL targets this input.

swapView.description: Read-only swap representation derived from the order side and limit price.

recipient.description: Recipient address supplied when creating the order.

refundTo.description: Refund address supplied when creating the order.

estimatedWithdrawFee.description: Withdrawal-fee estimate captured at creation, in destination-asset smallest units. It covers one withdrawal. The fee charged for each withdrawal may differ.

estimatedWithdrawFeeFormatted.description: Withdrawal-fee estimate formatted using the destination asset decimals.

estimatedRefundFee.description: Refund-fee estimate captured at creation, in input-asset smallest units. The fee charged for the refund may differ.

estimatedRefundFeeFormatted.description: Refund-fee estimate formatted using the input asset decimals.

timeInForce.description: Time in force for the order.

deadline.description: Timestamp in ISO format that identifies when the order can expire.

createdAt.description: Timestamp in ISO format that identifies when the order was created.

partialFills.description: Successful fills. Fills that are in flight or failed are not reported.

reason.description: Terminal failure reason. This payout leg is not retried. Not populated yet - reserved for a defined set of public reasons.

correlationId.description: Unique identifier for request tracing and debugging.

timestamp.description: Timestamp in ISO format when the response was generated.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page.

correlationId.description: Unique identifier for request tracing and debugging.

timestamp.description: Timestamp in ISO format when the response was generated.

pointer.description: JSON Pointer to the member of the request document that caused the error.

status.description: HTTP status code as a string, per JSON:API.

code.description: Stable machine-readable identifier. Branch on this, never on title or detail. New codes arrive without a major version, so treat an unrecognized code as the HTTP status alone. Each response documents the codes it can carry; this type is shared by every endpoint and so cannot list them.

detail.example: Must be a positive decimal string.

errors.description: Always populated, and never sent with data. One entry per failed field, so a request with several invalid attributes returns several errors. The codes an operation can return are listed in its description.

attached_deposit.description:
Optionally, attach deposit to [`.on_auth`](::defuse_auth_call::AuthCallee::on_auth) call. The amount will be subtracted from user's NEP-141 `wNEAR` balance.

NOTE: the `wNEAR` will not be refunded in case of fail.

contract_id.description: Callee for [`.on_auth`](::defuse_auth_call::AuthCallee::on_auth)

min_gas.description:
Optional minimum gas required for created promise to succeed. By default, only [`MIN_GAS_DEFAULT`](AuthCall::MIN_GAS_DEFAULT) is required.

Remaining gas will be distributed evenly across all Function Call Promises created during execution of current receipt.

msg.description: `msg` to pass in [`.on_auth`](::defuse_auth_call::AuthCallee::on_auth)

state_init.description: Optionally initialize the receiver's contract (Deterministic AccountId) via [`state_init`](https://github.com/near/NEPs/blob/master/neps/nep-0616.md#stateinit-action) right before calling [`.on_auth()`](::defuse_auth_call::AuthCallee::on_auth) (in the same receipt).

MultiPayload.description:
Assuming wallets want to interact with Intents protocol, besides preparing the data in a certain form, they have to have the capability to sign raw messages (off-chain signatures) using an algorithm we understand. This enum solves that problem.

For example, because we support ERC-191 and know how to verify messages with that standard, we can allow wallets, like Metamask, sign messages to perform intents without having to support new cryptographic primitives and signing standards.

Remaining gas will be distributed evenly across all Function Call Promises created during execution of current receipt.

msg.description: Message to pass to `ft_transfer_call`. Otherwise, `ft_transfer` will be used. NOTE: No refund will be made in case of insufficient `storage_deposit` on `token` for `receiver_id`

receiver_id.description:
NEAR Account Identifier.

This is a unique, syntactically valid, human-readable account identifier on the NEAR network.

[See the crate-level docs for information about validation.](index.html#account-id-rules)

Also see [Error kind precedence](AccountId#error-kind-precedence).

## Examples

``` use near_account_id::AccountId;

let alice: AccountId = "alice.near".parse().unwrap();

assert!("ƒelicia.near".parse::<AccountId>().is_err()); // (ƒ is not f) ```

storage_deposit.description: Optionally make `storage_deposit` for `receiver_id` on `token`. The amount will be subtracted from user's NEP-141 `wNEAR` balance. NOTE: the `wNEAR` will not be refunded in case of fail

PermissionedAccounts.description:
Collects super admin accounts and accounts that have been granted permissions defined by `AccessControlRole`.

# Data structure

Assume `AccessControlRole` is derived for the following enum, which is then passed as `role` attribute to `AccessControllable`.

```rust pub enum Role { PauseManager, UnpauseManager, } ```

Then the returned data has the following structure:

```ignore PermissionedAccounts { super_admins: vec!["acc1.near", "acc2.near"], roles: HashMap::from([ ("PauseManager", PermissionedAccountsPerRole { admins: vec!["acc3.near", "acc4.near"], grantees: vec!["acc5.near", "acc6.near"], }), ("UnpauseManager", PermissionedAccountsPerRole { admins: vec!["acc7.near", "acc8.near"], grantees: vec!["acc9.near", "acc10.near"], }), ]) } ```

# Uniqueness and ordering

Account ids returned in vectors are unique but not ordered.

StorageDeposit.description:
Make [NEP-145](https://nomicon.io/Standards/StorageManagement#nep-145) `storage_deposit` for an `account_id` on `contract_id`. The `amount` will be subtracted from user's NEP-141 `wNEAR` balance. NOTE: the `wNEAR` will not be refunded in any case.

WARNING: use this intent only if paying storage_deposit is not a prerequisite for other intents to succeed. If some intent (e.g. ft_withdraw) requires storage_deposit, then use storage_deposit field of corresponding intent instead of adding a separate `StorageDeposit` intent. This is due to the fact that intents that fire `Promise`s are not guaranteed to be executed sequentially, in the order of the provided intents in `DefuseIntents`.

Remaining gas will be distributed evenly across all Function Call Promises created during execution of current receipt.

msg.description: Message to pass to `nft_transfer_call`. Otherwise, `nft_transfer` will be used. NOTE: No refund will be made in case of insufficient `storage_deposit` on `token` for `receiver_id`

receiver_id.description:
NEAR Account Identifier.

This is a unique, syntactically valid, human-readable account identifier on the NEAR network.

[See the crate-level docs for information about validation.](index.html#account-id-rules)

Also see [Error kind precedence](AccountId#error-kind-precedence).

## Examples

``` use near_account_id::AccountId;

let alice: AccountId = "alice.near".parse().unwrap();

assert!("ƒelicia.near".parse::<AccountId>().is_err()); // (ƒ is not f) ```

storage_deposit.description: Optionally make `storage_deposit` for `receiver_id` on `token`. The amount will be subtracted from user's NEP-141 `wNEAR` balance. NOTE: the `wNEAR` will not be refunded in case of fail

Remaining gas will be distributed evenly across all Function Call Promises created during execution of current receipt.

msg.description: Message to pass to `nft_transfer_call`. Otherwise, `nft_transfer` will be used. NOTE: No refund will be made in case of insufficient `storage_deposit` on `token` for `receiver_id`

receiver_id.description:
NEAR Account Identifier.

This is a unique, syntactically valid, human-readable account identifier on the NEAR network.

[See the crate-level docs for information about validation.](index.html#account-id-rules)

Also see [Error kind precedence](AccountId#error-kind-precedence).

## Examples

``` use near_account_id::AccountId;

let alice: AccountId = "alice.near".parse().unwrap();

assert!("ƒelicia.near".parse::<AccountId>().is_err()); // (ƒ is not f) ```

storage_deposit.description: Optionally make `storage_deposit` for `receiver_id` on `token`. The amount will be subtracted from user's NEP-141 `wNEAR` balance. NOTE: the `wNEAR` will not be refunded in case of fail
